column7: A direct v3 native plug-in ABI owns bounded identity version capability lifecycle and loader metadata without accepting an older ABI
The public veriuser header declares standardized TF scalar types constants reasons value records globals and routine signatures with portable C and C++ linkage
Linux shared-library and Windows import-library surfaces expose the same standardized TF symbols calling convention and bounded discovery contract
The loader discovers one bounded direct-v3 table of standard TF registrations and rejects absent malformed duplicate or incompatible discovery metadata transactionally
Every task and function descriptor is fully validated and copied in source order before publication so one invalid field leaves no registration or callable residue
Standard checktf sizetf and calltf callbacks execute in their defined lifecycle with retained-image task and width-qualified function result ownership and contained failures
All standard misctf reasons preserve source registration order parameter-change identity synchronization distinctions retained-image lifetime and bounded exception or re-entry containment
Argument count type direction expression and width inspection shares one immutable call-site inventory across check size and call phases and rejects invalid access without mutation
Integer real string vector and expression reads and writes retain exact standardized value semantics including unknown and high-impedance state
Parameter and instance-specific access resolves against the active registered call context without crossing hierarchy generation or plug-in ownership
Simulation time delay scheduling and timescale queries use exact bounded conversions and preserve current instance time unit and precision
Scope instance work-area and user-data state has explicit plug-in call and elaborated-instance lifetime without stale or cross-run aliases
TF output warning error finish and stop controls publish deterministic simulator-owned effects with bounded formatting and stable failure diagnostics
Read-only and read-write synchronization requests retain generation-qualified instance order and execute with transactional observation and mutation boundaries
Registered TF system tasks and functions bind in every retained Verilog and SystemVerilog profile without changing language-profile selection
Every TF entry and callback crosses one scheduler coordinator that serializes plug-in effects while preserving deterministic simulator ordering
Plug-in exceptions invalid addresses unload and recursive entry fail within a governed boundary and cannot publish partial simulator state
Independently authored C and C++ TF plug-ins compile load execute and unload with equivalent observations on governed Linux and Windows toolchains
